sections.h2: Returns settle into a wide, persistent spread, not a tight band near zero

chart.title: The average spread sits near zero, but the 25th-75th percentile range is wide
chart.sub: ROIC minus cost of capital, percentage points, US public companies excluding financials, 1970-2024.
chart.source: Morgan Stanley Counterpoint Global Insights, Consilient Observer, 14 April 2026 (Exhibit 9).
ref: 0 = earns exactly its cost of capital

sections.means: The average company sat slightly below its cost of capital over five decades, with wide dispersion around that average.

sections.h2: Competitive advantage fades slowly, at 0.10-0.30 a year, not in one year

chart.title: Sector fade rates run 0.10-0.30 a year, far from full reversion in one year
chart.sub: Implied annual fade rate of the ROIC-cost of capital spread; 1.0 would mean full reversion within a year.
chart.source: Mauboussin and Callahan, Competitive Advantage Period, Counterpoint Global Insights, 14 April 2026 (Exhibit 11).

sections.means: On average about 79% of a company's deviation from average ROIC is still there the next year.
sections.todo: Treat any gap between returns and cost of capital as lasting years, not one planning cycle, when valuing a project.
